run.question: Someone changed the ConfigMap app-config in namespace cp1-mf recently. Show its current settings and tell me which field manager last modified it and when, and which manager created it.

report.summary: The ConfigMap cp1-mf/app-config exists and is currently carrying data CACHE_TTL_SECONDS="5" and LOG_LEVEL="info" (resourceVersion 4907, creationTimestamp 2026-11-23T15:17:52Z). Its managedFieldsSummary shows two managers: kubectl-create with its last write at 2026-11-23T15:17:52Z (identical to the object's creationTimestamp, i.e. consistent with creating the object) and cp1-release-bot with its last write at 2026-11-23T15:18:57Z, which is therefore the field manager that last modified the object, 65 seconds after creation. The Kubernetes view explicitly cannot say which fields that last write changed, and the change_history integration needed for a field-level diff is not integrated in this Run, so the previously stored values and the exact field edited are unknown. No pods or deployments consuming this ConfigMap were returned by the queries run (those queries returned no data, so this is a gap, not a healthy finding).

claims.text: ConfigMap cp1-mf/app-config currently holds exactly two data keys: CACHE_TTL_SECONDS="5" and LOG_LEVEL="info"; its metadata shows creationTimestamp 2026-11-23T15:17:52Z and resourceVersion "4907". No labels and no annotations are set on it.

The managedFieldsSummary of cp1-mf/app-config lists manager "cp1-release-bot" (operation Update) with last write time 2026-11-23T15:18:57Z — the most recent manager entry, so cp1-release-bot is the field manager that last modified the ConfigMap, about 65 seconds after its 15:17:52Z creation.

The only other manager entry on cp1-mf/app-config is "kubectl-create" (operation Update) with last write time 2026-11-23T15:17:52Z, which equals the ConfigMap's creationTimestamp 2026-11-23T15:17:52Z — consistent with kubectl-create having created the object.

The listing of ConfigMaps in namespace cp1-mf at query time returned two objects: app-config (created 2026-11-23T15:17:52Z) and kube-root-ca.crt (created 2026-11-23T15:17:52Z, managed by kube-controller-manager).

The 2026-11-23T15:18:57Z write by manager cp1-release-bot is the "recent change" referred to: it is the only write recorded after the object's creation, and its manager name indicates a release automation identity rather than a human operator. Which specific key (CACHE_TTL_SECONDS or LOG_LEVEL) it changed, and what the previous value was, cannot be established from managedFieldsSummary.

No ConfigMap-kind events appear in the grouped cluster-wide event summary inside the authorized window (groups cover DaemonSet, Deployment, Lease, Node, Pod, ReplicaSet and StatefulSet only), so events provide no corroboration of who or what changed cp1-mf/app-config; Kubernetes Event objects typically do not record ConfigMap edits.

To learn which keys changed and to what values before 2026-11-23T15:18:57Z, consult an audit-log / change-history source (the change_history integration is not connected in this Run); from the cluster API alone, compare a stored backup or Git manifest of cp1-mf/app-config against the current values CACHE_TTL_SECONDS="5" and LOG_LEVEL="info".

gaps: The change_history integration is listed as not integrated, so no field-level change history or audit trail of cp1-mf/app-config was available; the previously stored values and the exact field(s) cp1-release-bot modified at 2026-11-23T15:18:57Z are unknown.

metadata.managedFieldsSummary only preserves each manager's last write time and does not report which fields that write changed, so the diff between the kubectl-create state and the cp1-release-bot state cannot be derived.

The attribution of creation to "kubectl-create" rests on its summary entry's time equalling the object's creationTimestamp; the raw full managedFields entries were replaced by managedFieldsSummary in the tool output.

Queries for pods in namespace cp1-mf and for Deployments cluster-wide referencing a ConfigMap named app-config returned no data, so whether any workload consumes cp1-mf/app-config (and how it was affected) is unchecked, not shown to be absent; no pods were found in that namespace via the pod query.
next_steps: Enable or query the change_history / audit-log integration to retrieve the pre-change ConfigMap contents and the actor behind manager cp1-release-bot at 2026-11-23T15:18:57Z.

If impact matters, check whether any workload outside cp1-mf (StatefulSets, Jobs, DaemonSets, or pods mounting it as a volume/envFrom) references the ConfigMap name app-config and restarted around 2026-11-23T15:18:57Z.
